column1: # topic: Chapter 7: The American People and the American Revolution, 1775-1783

column2: On June 17, 1775, 1,600 rebels held Breed's Hill until their ammunition ran out, costing Britain 228 dead and 800 wounded.

column1: When the Second Continental Congress met
column2: It met on May 10, 1775, a month after Lexington and Concord.

column1: When the Olive Branch Petition was sent

column2: Dunmore offered freedom to slaves in November 1775.
Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776.
Perhaps one-fifth of the population backed the king in 1775.
At its peak Britain had 50,000 troops plus about 30,000 Hessians.

column1: When Trenton and Princeton were fought
column2: Washington took Trenton on Christmas night 1776 and won at Princeton on January 3, 1777.

column1: When France allied with the US
column2: France signed its alliance in early 1778, Spain joined less than a year later, and Britain was fighting the Dutch by 1780.
About 2,500 of 11,000 soldiers died at Valley Forge in winter 1777-78.
Charleston surrendered to the British on May 12, 1780.

column1: When King's Mountain and Cowpens were fought
column2: King's Mountain came in October 1780 and Cowpens in January 1781.

column1: When the Treaty of Paris was signed
column2: The Treaty of Paris was signed on September 3, 1783.
